# Introduction

`plot(aeme, "output")` and friends -- the S4 dispatcher used throughout the
other vignettes -- cover the common case. Underneath it, AEME ships a wider
set of purpose-built plotting functions: multi-variable timeseries, group
plots for individual biogeochemical modules, residuals against observations,
and diagnostics on the inputs (hypsograph, meteorology, flows) rather than
the output. This vignette works through them using one small built model.

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(AEME)
library(ggplot2)
options(AEME.inform = FALSE)
```

```{r build, message = FALSE, results = "hide", warning = FALSE}
aeme_file <- system.file("extdata/aeme.rds", package = "AEME")
aeme <- readRDS(aeme_file)

model_controls <- get_model_controls(use_bgc = TRUE)
model <- "glm_aed"
path <- tempdir()

aeme <- build_aeme(path = path, aeme = aeme, model = model,
                   model_controls = model_controls, ext_elev = 5,
                   use_bgc = TRUE)
aeme <- run_aeme(aeme = aeme, verbose = FALSE)
```

# Timeseries

`plot_ts()` is the general-purpose multi-variable plot -- pass one or more
`var_sim`, and it facets automatically. Observations overlay by default
(`add_obs = TRUE`) where the `Aeme` object has them.

```{r plot-ts}
plot_ts(aeme, model = model, var_sim = c("HYD_temp", "CHM_oxy"))
```

Restrict to a depth range (e.g. surface only) with `depth_range`:

```{r plot-ts-depth}
plot_ts(aeme, model = model, var_sim = "HYD_temp", depth_range = c(0, 2))
```

`plot_var()` is the lower-level building block `plot_ts()` is written on top
of -- reach for it directly when you already have a `data.frame` from
`get_var()` and want the same plot style without re-deriving it from the
`Aeme` object:

```{r plot-var}
df <- get_var(aeme, model = model, var_sim = "HYD_temp", return_df = TRUE)
plot_var(df = df, aeme = aeme, model = model, var_sim = "HYD_temp")
```

# Observations and residuals

`plot_obs()` shows the observation record alone -- useful for checking
coverage before deciding what to calibrate against (see also
`summarise_obs()` in `vignette("setup-new-lake")`):

```{r plot-obs}
plot_obs(aeme, var_sim = "HYD_temp")
```

`plot_resid()` plots modelled-minus-observed directly, rather than the two
series overlaid -- the faster way to see whether a model is biased high/low
versus just imprecise:

```{r plot-resid}
plot_resid(aeme, model = model, var_sim = "HYD_temp")
```

# Biogeochemical group plots

Each major AED module has its own plot, all sharing the `plot_ts()`
argument shape (`add_obs`, `depth_range`, `remove_spin_up`, `ens_n`):

```{r plot-nit}
plot_nit(aeme)
```

```{r plot-phs}
plot_phs(aeme)      # phosphorus
```

```{r plot-car}
plot_car(aeme)      # carbon
```

```{r plot-phytos}
plot_phytos(aeme)   # phytoplankton groups
```
Similarly, `plot_zoops()` shows the zooplankton groups but requires the 
zooplankton module to be active in the model configuration. This example's 
minimal config does not carry zooplankton/full phyto groups.

```{r plot-zoops, eval = FALSE}
plot_zoops(aeme)    # zooplankton groups
```

# Inputs, not output

Three functions plot what went *into* the model rather than what came out --
useful when a run looks wrong and the question is whether the forcing data
is the problem.

Meteorology, as a tile plot (one row per variable, coloured by value,
faceted by hydrological year):

```{r plot-met-tile}
plot_met_tile(aeme, var_inp = "MET_tmpair")
```

The hypsograph the model was built with:

```{r plot-hyps}
plot_hyps(aeme)
```

Inflows and/or outflows:

```{r plot-flows}
plot_flows(aeme, flow = "inflow")
```

Cumulative heat fluxes (e.g. checking an energy budget):

```{r plot-fluxes}
plot_fluxes(aeme, cumulative = TRUE)
```

# Working with a raw output list

`plot_model_output()` is the lowest-level of the plotting functions: pass it
an `Aeme` object directly, as below, or -- its other accepted input -- the
specifically classed list `read_glm_output()`/`read_gotm_output()`/
`read_simstrat_output()`/`read_dy_output()`/`read_model_outputs()` return
(`output(aeme)` itself is a plain list and isn't accepted; use one of those
readers if you need output outside the `Aeme` object). It's what every
other `plot_*` function on this page is ultimately built on:

```{r get-model-outfile}
outfile <- get_model_outfile(aeme, model = "glm_aed")$glm_aed
outfile
```

`read_glm_output()` reads the model output, projects onto a standard grid
and also does some unit conversions, especially for the AED variables that are 
stored in mmol/m3 in the raw output but are more commonly expressed in mg/L.

```{r plot-model-output}
out <- read_glm_output(file = outfile)
plot_model_output(out, var_sim = "CHM_oxy")
```

However, you can also load all raw output from the GLM netcdf output file and 
plot any variable in its raw form e.g. model units and Lagrangian grid, rather 
than the standardised grid and converted units. This is useful for plotting 
variables that are not included in the `Aeme` object by default.
You need to use the raw variable name for plotting instead of the standardised
AEME variable name.

```{r}
raw <- read_glm_output(file = outfile, raw = TRUE, load_all = TRUE)
raw
```

```{r}
plot_model_output(raw, var_sim = "OXY_oxy")
```



The AED sediment fluxes, which are not included in the `Aeme` object by default.
For example, to plot the sediment oxygen flux:

```{r}
plot_model_output(raw, var_sim = "SDF_Fsed_oxy_Z")
```

# A lightweight summary for dashboards

The depth-resolved output of a model run is large, and most dashboards only
need a few series. `summarise_aeme()` (also what `summary(aeme)` returns)
reduces an `Aeme` to an `AemeSummary`: daily surface and bottom values for every
depth-resolved variable, the variables that have no depth, and optionally the
observations, daily forcing and the hypsograph. It holds no model
configuration, so it cannot be built or run -- it is only for looking at.

```{r summarise}
aeme_summ <- summarise_aeme(aeme)
aeme_summ
```

The `output` is a plain long table, so it goes straight into ggplot2, a
dashboard, or any other language. `layer` is `"surface"` or `"bottom"` (split at
the epilimnion depth, `HYD_epidep`, else the thermocline depth, else half the
water column), or `NA` for variables without depth. `stat` is `"value"` for a
single run; with an ensemble it holds the statistics across members (mean, min,
max and the 5th/95th percentiles by default).

```{r summary-output}
head(output(aeme_summ))
```

`plot()` and `get_var()` work on a summary, and the same accessors you use on an
`Aeme` (`lake()`, `time()`, `observations()`, `parameters()`) apply, with
`forcing()`, `hypsograph()`, `profiles()` and `models()` for the rest:

```{r summary-plot}
plot(aeme_summ, "HYD_temp")
```

```{r summary-forcing}
names(forcing(aeme_summ))
head(forcing(aeme_summ)$meteo)
```

It is a fraction of the size of the full object:

```{r summary-size}
format(object.size(aeme_summ), units = "Kb")
format(object.size(aeme), units = "Kb")
```

Store it with `write_aeme_summary()` -- `"rds"` (the default), `"parquet"` (one
file per table, for dashboards in other tools) or `"json"` -- and read it back
with `read_aeme_summary()` (`rds` and `parquet`):

```{r summary-write}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
write_aeme_summary(aeme_summ, f)
aeme_summ2 <- read_aeme_summary(f)
identical(output(aeme_summ2), output(aeme_summ))
```

For an ensemble (see `run_aeme_ensemble()`), `summarise_aeme()` combines the
members into the statistics in `stats`, and `keep_members = TRUE` keeps each
member's series as well. Arguments such as `vars`, `observations`, `forcing`
and `profiles` choose what goes in, so a summary can be made as small as the
dashboard needs.
